t.6.19.1: Having heard the words of Sāraṇa, Śuka, surveying the whole army, then spoke these words to Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas.
t.6.19.2: Those whom you see standing here, like great elephants in rut, like banyan trees growing on the banks of the Gaṅgā, like sāla trees of the Himālaya,
t.6.19.3: These, O king, are hard to withstand, mighty, and able to take any form at will; resembling the Daityas and Dānavas, they possess the valour of the gods in battle.
t.6.19.4: Of these there are nine, five and seven thousands of koṭis, and likewise thousands of śaṅkhas, and likewise hundreds of vṛndas.
t.6.19.5: These monkeys, ministers of Sugrīva, ever dwelling in Kiṣkindhā, were begotten by gods and gandharvas and can take on any form at will.
t.6.19.6: Those two youths whom you see standing there, godlike in form, are both Mainda and Dvivida; there is no one equal to them in battle.
t.6.19.8: Those two who stand at the side of these two, resembling mountains, are Sumukha and Vimukha, the sons of Mṛtyu, equal to their father.
t.6.19.7: These two, both of whom drank amṛta with Brahmā's permission, hope to crush Laṅkā in battle by their might.
t.6.19.9: But that monkey whom you see standing there like an elephant in rut, he who, when enraged, could by his strength churn up even the ocean,
t.6.19.10: This is the one who came to Laṅkā, to Vaidehī and to you, O lord. Behold this monkey, seen here before, who has now come back again.
t.6.19.11: He is the eldest son of Kesarin, known as the son of the Wind, renowned by the name Hanūmān; it was by him that the ocean was leapt across.
t.6.19.12: This best of monkeys can assume any form at will and is endowed with strength and beauty; his course cannot be checked, like that of the mighty, ever-moving Wind.
t.6.19.13: It is said that once, as a thirsty child, on seeing the rising sun, he crossed a distance of three thousand yojanas.
t.6.19.14: "I shall seize the sun, for my hunger will not go away," so this one, long ago, thought to himself in his mind, puffed up with pride in his strength.
t.6.19.15: Without ever reaching that god, who is utterly unassailable even by the gods, the divine seers and the Dānavas, he fell upon the mountain where the sun rises.
t.6.19.16: When this firm-jawed monkey fell, one of his jaws was slightly broken on the surface of a rock; for that reason he is indeed called Hanumān.
t.6.19.18: And this one next to him, the valiant hero, dark in complexion, with eyes like lotuses, is a peerless chariot-warrior among the Ikṣvākus, whose manly prowess is renowned throughout the world.
t.6.19.17: Truly, this monkey is known to me through report; his strength, his form and his power cannot be described. Alone, by his might, he hopes to crush Laṅkā.
t.6.19.20: He who could pierce the sky with his arrows and split the mountains as well, whose wrath is like that of Death and whose valour is like that of Śakra.
t.6.19.19: He in whom dharma never wavers, who never transgresses dharma, who knows the Brāhma weapon and the Vedas, he is the foremost among the knowers of the Vedas.
t.6.19.21: He whose wife Sītā was carried off by you from Janasthāna, that very Rāma, O king, is advancing to fight you.
t.6.19.22: And he who stands here on the right side, shining like pure jāmbūnada gold, broad-chested, with coppery eyes and dark, curling hair,
t.6.19.23: This is his brother, Lakṣmaṇa by name, dear to him as his own life, skilled in statecraft and in war, and learned in all the śāstras.
t.6.19.25: For he does not guard his own life in the cause of Rāghava; he indeed longs to slay all the rākṣasas in battle.
t.6.19.24: Indignant at wrong, hard to conquer, victorious, valorous, wise and mighty, he is Rāma's right arm, forever his very life-breath walking outside his body.
t.6.19.26: But that one who stands having taken his place on the left flank of Rāma, surrounded by a host of rākṣasas, is indeed King Vibhīṣaṇa.
t.6.19.27: Consecrated as king in Laṅkā by the glorious king of kings, this one, enraged, advances to battle against you alone.
t.6.19.28: But he whom you see standing in the middle, immovable like a mountain, is the unconquered lord of all the chiefs of the monkeys.
t.6.19.29: He who, by his splendour, glory, intelligence, knowledge and noble lineage, outshone the monkeys as the Himavān outshines the other mountains.
t.6.19.30: He who dwells, together with the chief leaders of the troops, in Kiṣkindhā, a cave thick with dense trees, impregnable and set within a mountain fastness.
t.6.19.31: He on whom this golden garland of a hundred lotuses shines, a garland beloved of gods and men in which Lakṣmī herself abides…
t.6.19.32: This garland, and Tārā, and the everlasting kingdom of the monkeys were bestowed upon Sugrīva by Rāma after he had slain Vālin.
t.6.19.34: O great king, having observed this army that has arrived, resembling blazing planets, let the utmost effort then be made, so that there may be victory and not defeat at the hands of the enemy.
t.6.19.33: Thus, with a thousand koṭis and a hundred śaṅkus of warriors, Sugrīva, the lord of the monkeys, is advancing against you to give battle.
